subsystems.name: Carbon-fixation enzyme module
subsystems.role: the core chemistry that turns CO2 into organic carbon.

subsystems.name: CO2-concentrating mechanism
subsystems.role: raises CO2 around the fixing enzyme so it stops wasting effort on oxygen.

subsystems.name: Energy and reducing-power supply
subsystems.role: pays the ATP and electron cost of fixation, which is very high.
parts: hydrogen or direct electron feed (for fermenter hosts)

subsystems.name: Host chassis
subsystems.role: the cell that carries the engineered pathways.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and gas exchange
subsystems.role: gets CO2 dissolved into liquid fast enough to feed the cells.
parts: CO2 feed from flue gas or air

subsystems.name: Carbon product and lock-up route
subsystems.role: keeps the captured carbon out of the atmosphere for a long time.

subsystems.name: Biocontainment and control
subsystems.role: stops engineered organisms escaping or outcompeting wild ones.

buildSteps.title: Pick the host and the chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Researchers compare natural and synthetic fixation cycles, then choose a chassis — a cyanobacterium, a fast-growing bacterium, yeast, or a crop plant — that can plausibly run it.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a fixation cycle
buildSteps.detail: Genes for carboxylases and reductases are introduced, often in a synthetic cycle that avoids wasteful side reactions or uses less ATP than natural photosynthesis.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the CO2-concentrating mechanism
buildSteps.detail: Shell proteins, carbonic anhydrase and bicarbonate pumps are added so CO2 is funnelled straight to the fixing enzyme, reducing losses to oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Rewire central metabolism
buildSteps.detail: The cell's own metabolism is edited so it can only grow by fixing CO2, making faster fixation the only route to survival.

buildSteps.title: Evolve it in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Cultures are grown under controlled CO2 and light, with the fastest-growing variants selected over many generations — directed evolution rather than design alone.

buildSteps.title: Couple in the energy source
buildSteps.detail: Light, or hydrogen or electricity from an electrolyser, is supplied at the rate the cycle needs; oxygen and heat must be managed at the same time.

buildSteps.title: Scale the reactor
buildSteps.detail: The system moves from flasks to photobioreactors or fermenters, where the hard limit becomes how quickly CO2 can be dissolved into liquid.

buildSteps.title: Lock the carbon away
buildSteps.detail: Harvested carbon is turned into a durable product, charred, buried or mineralised, and its long-term stability is measured — otherwise the sink leaks.

prerequisites.why: RuBisCO is among the slowest enzymes known and is easily confused by oxygen; improved variants work only in the lab so far.
carboxysomes work in bacteria, but transferring the full system into crops or industrial microbes is unfinished.
editing and controlling cyanobacteria, algae and E. coli is routine, though slower-growing autotrophs are harder.
kill switches and dependency on an added nutrient are demonstrated but not proven over years outdoors.
the process needs large energy inputs, so it only helps the climate if that energy is clean.
geological storage, biochar and long-lived materials already exist, though at limited scale.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of synthetic fixation cycles and engineered autotrophs achieving measurable, if slow, CO2-dependent growth
pathway.unlocks: proof the chemistry can be rewired at all.

pathway.milestone: pilot bioreactors fed with real flue gas, showing reliable fixation over months
pathway.unlocks: a realistic cost and energy figure for the approach.

pathway.milestone: contained field trials and products whose carbon stays locked up for decades
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the sink is real, not temporary.

pathway.milestone: deployment where it beats other carbon-removal options on cost and energy
pathway.unlocks: a contributor to mitigation, most likely as a niche alongside direct air capture and point-source capture.
